title.value: CrossSplit: Mitigating Label Noise Memorization through Data Splitting
title.justification: The title effectively captures the essence of the paper, which introduces a method called CrossSplit to tackle the challenge of label noise memorization in deep learning models.
title.quote: CrossSplit: Mitigating Label Noise Memorization through Data Splitting

extractions.description: The paper introduces CrossSplit, a novel approach to mitigating label noise memorization in deep learning. It involves splitting labeled data into two disjoint parts and training separate neural networks on each part, using a cross-split label correction mechanism. The method enhances robustness against noisy labels by leveraging peer network predictions for label correction and semi-supervised learning techniques.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving the robustness of deep learning methods to label noise rather than addressing an eco-responsible topic.
primary_category.quote: We approach the problem of improving robustness of deep learning algorithms in the presence of label noise.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not delve into any secondary eco-responsible categories; it is mainly concerned with methodological improvements in machine learning.
secondary_categories.quote: Our contributions are summarized as follows: We introduce CrossSplit for robust training.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since there is no direct eco-responsible application or implication of the method discussed, no specific sub-category fits.
primary_sub_category.quote: The goal of this paper is to propose a novel robust training scheme that addresses some of these drawbacks.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not engage with sub-categories as its focus is on a methodological improvement unrelated to eco-responsibility.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This procedure allows us to avoid the memorization of examples without significantly degrading the learning of difficult examples.

applications.justification: The primary application discussed in the paper is the mitigation of label noise memorization in machine learning models, which is a methodological improvement rather than an eco-responsible application.
applications.quote: We approach the problem of improving robustness of deep learning algorithms in the presence of label noise.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper introduces a new training paradigm (CrossSplit) to enhance the robustness of models against label noise, a methodological improvement rather than a contribution to an existing eco-responsible category.
new_primary_category.quote: CrossSplit combines two main ingredients: (i) Cross-split label correction... (ii) Cross-split semi-supervised training.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no need for a new sub-category since the primary category itself is sufficiently explanatory in this context.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The idea is to bypass the sample selection process by using a random splitting of the data into two disjoints parts, and to train a separate network on each of these splits.
